blocks.text: Disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of upper airway obstruction during sleep, resulting in interrupted ventilation, intermittent hypoxia, and sleep fragmentation. Laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPR) with/without Vocal cord nodules or Laryngeal polyp)
Occurs when gastric contents reach the larynx, affecting the glottis and vocal cords.
It commonly presents with hoarseness, globus sensation, chronic throat clearing, and sometimes heartburn or regurgitation.
Unlike gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which involves the lower esophageal sphincter, LPR is linked to dysfunction of the upper esophageal sphincter.
